candidates.statement: Gateway checkout returns 502 because its downstream call to order POST /v1/orders returns HTTP 500. Traces and logs show the gateway's client request to order failing with 500, propagating as 502 on /v1/checkout.
candidates.uncertainty: Order-side root cause (db, redis, payment) not observed; only gateway-side evidence available.

report.explanation: Gateway 502s on /v1/checkout are caused by the order service returning 500 on POST /v1/orders, as seen in correlated traces and client-request logs. The specific order-side fault is not yet established, so the bounded candidate is the propagated HTTP 500.
missing_evidence: Order service traces/logs showing the internal cause of its 500 on POST /v1/orders
Order dependency metrics (postgresql, payment, inventory) to rule out db-pool-exhaustion or downstream-latency
